observations.explanation: The paper describes APIBench across HuggingFace, TorchHub, and TensorHub, then fine-tunes Gorilla with and without retrieval and reports results across zero-shot and retriever settings (PDF pp. 2, 4–7).

The evaluation uses AST matching against the collected API dataset (PDF pp. 5–6), and the appendix says code execution results were not tested (PDF p. 13). The paper therefore does not establish successful execution or semantic correctness in actual use.

The paper says the holdout was made by dividing instruction/API pairs into training and testing sets (PDF p. 6), while the appendix reports splits by dataset entries but does not establish that APIs themselves were held out (PDF p. 13). It is reasonable to identify API-level generalization as unresolved.

For HuggingFace, the paper says that all models except Gorilla are checked only for correct domain names, reducing that evaluation to multiple choice (PDF p. 7). The claim accurately notes the comparison is nonuniform and that its impact is unclear.
